source.title: Bounding generalization error with input compression: An empirical study with infinite-width networks
source.authors: A. Galloway; A. Golubeva; Mahmoud Salem; M. Nica; Yani Ioannou; Graham W. Taylor

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extracting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Uses a different measurement and model family to study generalization gaps, label randomization, and which measured property tracks the gap. It does not test the versions’ specified finite-width architectures or training recipes directly.
record.gate_note: The study’s own results bear on V1 through its random-label training and natural-label accuracy comparisons, and V7 through its comparison of input-compression bounds with measured generalization error. Results about the ICB as a bound or ranking measure are included where they measure the gap named by those versions. Other claim versions are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study tests V1 using infinite-width fully connected networks: the same EuroSAT model and regularization setting fit natural and randomized labels perfectly, with natural-label test accuracy of 97.5% and random-label test accuracy of 50.0%. It does not test V7: input-compression mutual information is a different construct from magnitude-aware weight sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion. They argue that input compression provides a useful, non-vacuous generalization bound for infinite-width networks, detects label randomization and robust-generalization failures, and offers a more effective complexity metric than parameter count or depth. They acknowledge variable coverage and ranking performance and caution against extrapolation to finite-width networks.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses infinite-width neural networks trained by full-batch gradient descent and evaluates an input-compression mutual-information bound; it does not reproduce the finite-width model, architecture, optimizer, or sharpness procedures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Coverage and ranking vary by dataset, binary task, training accuracy, activation function, training regime, and metaparameter range. Larger diagonal regularization reduces ICB in the illustrative experiment; rankings vary when several metaparameters vary.

fits_no_version.finding: ICB coverage varies substantially across datasets, tasks and accuracy restrictions, including rates far below nominal 95% coverage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-compression bounds have task- and model-dependent empirical coverage in infinite-width image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: ICB positively ranks generalization gaps among perfectly fitted models, but its ranking against a training-accuracy baseline varies by dataset and experimental regime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-compression bounds can track generalization gaps in infinite-width networks, with ranking quality depending on the comparison set.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to infinite-width networks and binary image-classification tasks; the authors caution that extrapolation to finite-width DNNs is uncertain. Some satisfaction rates are far below the nominal ≈95% level. The paper’s random-label table does not provide held-out accuracy for randomized-label training. No direct magnitude-aware sharpness, norm- or margin-based comparison, width sweep, or finite-width architecture comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: The article reports many additional per-dataset, per-task and per-metric correlation values in Tables A6–A10 and Figure A12. These are not expanded into separate rows because the extracted rows capture the overall comparisons and key conditions where outcomes vary; the paper’s table-level aggregates are stated directly where used. No figure-only values were transcribed.

untested.parts: The original finite-width architectures, multiclass CIFAR-10 and ImageNet tasks, and training without explicit regularization are untested. The direct comparison uses an infinite-width two-layer ReLU network with diagonal regularization.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the interpolation width.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparison or tuning comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, sharpness-gap correlation, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V1 limits_scope verdict based on supposedly missing random-label test accuracy: Table 2 supplies it. Remove all V7 verdicts because ICB is a different measure. Untested architectures and recipes do not themselves justify limits_scope.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test small Inception, AlexNet, or MLPs on CIFAR-10; Inception V3 on ImageNet; or the exact Zhang et al. setup. Uses infinite-width fully connected networks on five binary image-classification tasks. Does not report held-out accuracy under randomized labels as a primary comparison; its table reports training accuracy, test accuracy, and GE for a EuroSAT task.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures.
Uses full-batch gradient descent and does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not compare batch sizes or fixed-epoch large-batch recipes.

Measures input-to-representation mutual information and its derived bound, not magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness. Its correlations concern infinite-width networks, binary image tasks, and clean or perturbed test sets; it does not evaluate the norm- and margin-based comparisons named in the version.
Does not remove selected memorized examples or compare retraining against random-example removal.
